text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَوْ تَرَىٰٓ إِذْ فَزِعُوا۟ فَلَا فَوْتَ وَأُخِذُوا۟ مِن مَّكَانٍۢ قَرِيبٍۢ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction joined to the suspended conditional opening

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: conditional particle joined to the opening conjunction

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) begins by carrying the previous warning into the suspended vision rather than opening an isolated scene. Because it is joined directly to {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}), continuity and conditional suspension arrive as one compact onset, and the clipped opening cadence moves quickly from linkage into the longer seeing verb.

topics.headline: resumption before the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah’s spectacle is grammatically attached to the prior warning frame before the vision begins.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar allows coordination or resumption, and the local clause structure makes the particle part of the suspended seeing clause.

topics.headline: connector fused to conditional onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the connector is heard and written as part of the rapid {{ar:وَ لَوْ}} ({{tr:wa law}}) launch, not as a detachable preface.
topics.reason: The surface particle is prefixed to the conditional particle, so the formal and acoustic rows are locally coherent.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle opening an unreal or rhetorically suspended vision frame
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) suspends the scene as an unreal witnessing frame whose full answer is left compressed. The following panic, no-escape verdict, and seizure therefore have to carry the answer themselves, making the addressee dwell inside the vision rather than receive a settled explanatory clause. In the boundary from 34:50, this keeps the warning continuous while changing it into staged sight.

topics.headline: unspoken answer carried by the scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the missing answer after the condition makes the scene itself function as the withheld consequence.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly marks the answer as suspended after the conditional opening, so the compression is licensed locally.

topics.headline: condition becomes visual warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the conditional is not ordinary narrative but an invitation to imagine seeing the judgment scene.
topics.reason: The conditional governs the seeing frame, and the boundary rows coherently connect the prior warning to a visual disclosure.

words.gloss_range: second masculine singular seeing/perceiving verb with the viewed scene left as the following event complex
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, perceiving, recognizing, and judging; locally the addressee is made to witness and understand the scene

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: temporal scene marker introducing the viewed panic moment

words.prose: {{ar:تَرَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tarā}}) places a singular addressed witness outside the plural group that will panic and be seized. Its object is not named; the following {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) scene becomes what is seen, so sight expands into perception of panic, abolished escape, and capture as one configuration. The imperfect form keeps the witnessing open, while the root’s seeing-and-judging range makes the spectacle an act of recognition, not bare looking.

topics.headline: outside witness sees the whole event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressee is grammatically outside the doomed plural group and that the whole following event becomes the object of sight.
topics.reason: The verb is 2MS with no direct object, while the later panic and seizure verbs are 3MP, supporting both outside vantage and scene-object compression.

topics.headline: seeing includes recognition of judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vision asks for understanding the inevitability of the sequence, not curiosity about a spectacle.
topics.reason: The root field supports seeing and judging, and the local seen content is the no-escape sequence rather than a neutral object.

topics.headline: unfolding witness with indirect showing force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form directly addresses the witness’s seeing and keeps it unfolding, while any causative showing force comes from the frame rather than the verb form itself.
topics.reason: The surface is active Form I in the local grammar, so rows invoking a causative showing field are preserved only as contextual pressure, not as the selected morphology.

topics.headline: judgment warning turns into sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah moves from the prior speech register into a vision formula where failed evasion becomes visible.
topics.reason: The cross-passage and boundary rows are coherent with the local {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) plus seeing frame and do not control the local parse beyond that formulaic contrast.

words.gloss_range: temporal scene marker attaching the panic moment to the seeing frame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: seeing verb governing the temporal scene
panic event inside the temporal window

words.prose: {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) fastens the witnessing to the moment of panic. It is governed by {{ar:تَرَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tarā}}), so {{ar:فَزِعُوا۟}} ({{tr:faziʿū}}) supplies the event inside the viewed time-window rather than taking over the whole construction. The particle turns time into a hinge: suspended address becomes event sequence, and the panic feels fixed enough to be inspected.

topics.headline: seeing fixed to the panic instant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah directs attention to the onset of collapse as the seen moment, not to a broad background narrative.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the temporal phrase depend on the seeing verb, with the panic event inside that window.

topics.headline: time turns into consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the time-marker is the pivot from suspended vision into the sequence that will produce no escape.
topics.reason: The clause following the particle feeds the result clause, so the structural hinge rows are locally supported.

words.gloss_range: active perfect plural panic, locally intransitive and not directed toward refuge
words.root_gloss_range: sudden alarm, fright, and in some constructions rushing for aid; local grammar selects alarm without directed recourse
words.prose: {{ar:فَزِعُوا۟}} ({{tr:faziʿū}}) is the first event inside the viewed moment, and it is active perfect plural: the group still appears as actors, but the only action left to them is panic. The verb is intransitive here, with no ilā preposition directing fear toward aid or refuge, so the wider aid-rush branch is narrowed to alarm without recourse. Its same-surah contrast with terror removed in 34:23 sharpens the local point: this panic remains attached until {{ar:فَلَا فَوْتَ}} ({{tr:fa-lā fawta}}) and passive seizure overtake it. The f-z-ʿ sound tightens into final ʿayn, so the word itself helps the panic feel like a bodily constriction before the verdict.

topics.headline: last active predicate is panic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doomed group still receives an active verb, but that active role is reduced to completed panic.
topics.reason: The local verb is active perfect 3MP and the following seizure is passive 3MP, supporting the agency-collapse contrast.

topics.headline: alarm has no directed recourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root’s aid-rush possibility is blocked locally, leaving terror with no grammatical path toward refuge.
topics.reason: The verb instance has no object or preposition, and no {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}) follows it, so aid-seeking senses are kept only as a contrast to the selected intransitive panic.

topics.headline: same-surah terror contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same surah can show terror removed from hearts (34:23), whereas here panic remains unreleased before capture.
topics.reason: The same-root contrast is concrete and locally relevant because the surface here is active panic, not removal from terror.

topics.headline: panic tightens before the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices panic as a sudden bodily jolt whose sound and placement leave no interval for useful action.
topics.reason: The rows about sudden alarm, constricted sound, and location before the result particle are coherent with the local sequence.

words.gloss_range: result particle binding the panic beat to the no-escape verdict

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negator fused after the result particle

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the no-escape clause the immediate consequence of panic. Attached to {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), it removes narrative space between alarm and verdict: the ayah moves at once from what they do to what is no longer possible. Even the clipped-to-long sound of {{ar:فَلَا}} ({{tr:fa-lā}}) lets quick sequence open into sustained negation.

topics.headline: panic becomes verdict without delay
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that fear does not introduce a pause for response; it is converted immediately into the no-escape verdict.
topics.reason: The result clause begins with this particle after the panic event, so immediate consequence is locally licensed.

topics.headline: result fused to negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sequence and negation are encountered as one tight surface onset before the escape noun appears.
topics.reason: The particle is prefixed to the negator, preserving the formal and recitational payoff without making a separate lexical claim.

words.gloss_range: lā of categorical negation before the accusative verbal noun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: escape noun negated by lā of genus

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is not a narrow verbal negation. Before accusative {{ar:فَوْتَ}} ({{tr:fawta}}), it denies the whole genus of escape and leaves the verdict compressed, with the predicate unspoken. The verbless phrase interrupts the active panic and the passive seizure, forcing the event chain through an absolute category-denial before action resumes.

topics.headline: the escape category is abolished
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah denies escape as a category, not merely one failed attempt to get away.
topics.reason: Attachment and translation-support evidence identify the construction as categorical negation before the accusative verbal noun.

topics.headline: two-word verdict interrupts the verbs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah pauses verbal action into a terse nominal verdict before the seizure is reported.
topics.reason: The omitted predicate and nominal placement between two perfect verbs support the compression and interruption rows.

words.gloss_range: accusative verbal noun naming escape or slipping away as the category being negated
words.root_gloss_range: passing beyond reach, escaping, missed timing, and gap; local construction denies the whole escape category

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: final nearness adjective that closes escape-distance

words.prose: {{ar:فَوْتَ}} ({{tr:fawta}}) names escape as an abstract category under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), then lets that category be abolished. The root field includes slipping away and missed timing, so the verdict closes both space and opportunity; later {{ar:قَرِيبٍۢ}} ({{tr:qarībin}}) explains why no gap for evasion exists. The sparse bare gerund gives the two-word formula a legally terse feel, so the ayah sounds less like ordinary motion vocabulary than a compact ruling. Variant rows are useful by contrast: the canonical wording keeps the denial as a noun and the taking as the next passive event, not a localized temporal phrase or a second nominal outcome.

topics.headline: escape is negated as a category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not narrate an attempted escape; it names the possibility of escape and cancels it absolutely.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative under categorical {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), and the form is a verbal noun rather than a finite escape verb.

topics.headline: no spatial or temporal gap remains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that failed evasion is about both distance and timing: the gap through which escape would pass is closed before seizure is named.
topics.reason: The root rows about escape, missed chance, and gap are locally supported by the following near-source phrase and the no-escape construction.

topics.headline: canonical denial kept distinct from seizure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted variant contrasts sharpen the canonical text: escape-denial stays unlocalized and seizure remains a passive event.
topics.reason: The variant rows are valid apparatus, but the canonical surface has bare {{ar:فَوْتَ}} ({{tr:fawta}}) followed by passive {{ar:أُخِذُوا۟}} ({{tr:ukhidhū}}), so their force is contrastive rather than controlling.

topics.headline: sparse lexeme gives terse verdict force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compactness of the rare gerundal no-escape formula as a marked verdict rather than ordinary motion vocabulary.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence marks the exact gerundal form as low-occurrence and negated, supporting the distributional and terse-form rows.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction linking the no-escape verdict to passive seizure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: passive seizure verb after the connector

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links the passive seizure to the no-escape verdict instead of restarting the story. After the verbless {{ar:لَا فَوْتَ}} ({{tr:lā fawta}}), it reopens finite action through {{ar:أُخِذُوا۟}} ({{tr:ukhidhū}}), so abstract impossibility becomes visible execution without a delay particle.

topics.headline: seizure accompanies no escape
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that taking is coordinated with the no-escape verdict as its accompanying outcome, not introduced as an unrelated new scene.
topics.reason: The local clause evidence coordinates the passive event with the result clause, matching the additive and circumstantial rows.

topics.headline: connector attaches to passive verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the passive event arrives already joined to the prior verdict at the surface level.
topics.reason: The conjunction is prefixed directly to the passive verb, so the formal row is locally supported.

words.gloss_range: perfect passive plural seizure with the taker omitted and the patients foregrounded
words.root_gloss_range: taking, grasping, seizing, adopting, and holding accountable; local passive selects imposed capture after no escape
words.prose: {{ar:أُخِذُوا۟}} ({{tr:ukhidhū}}) completes the collapse of agency. The same plural group that actively panicked is now the passive patient, and the taker is grammatically omitted. The root’s taking and punitive grasp range fits its place after {{ar:لَا فَوْتَ}} ({{tr:lā fawta}}): once the escape gap is denied, the grasp closes. The hamza onset makes the return from nominal verdict to event sound like an impact at the seizure verb itself. Rows that point to named divine taking elsewhere, such as 11:102, are best kept as boundary pressure: the discourse can make the agent recoverable, but the local form still withholds the taker from the surface.

topics.headline: capture complete inside the vision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that capture is shown as already accomplished, with the seized group foregrounded and the taker absent from the grammar.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect passive 3MP with an omitted agent, so the completion and patient-focus rows are directly licensed.

topics.headline: active panic becomes passive patienthood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the morphological reversal from actors of panic to patients of seizure, making loss of control audible in the repeated plural ending.
topics.reason: The same 3MP group is carried from active panic to passive seizure, so the voice-role contrast is locally coherent.

topics.headline: taking as grasp and accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the taking is not neutral movement; after no escape it reads as capture with accountability pressure.
topics.reason: The root range supports taking, punitive seizure, and holding accountable, and the local passive follows the no-escape verdict.

topics.headline: seizure is visible and spatially sourced
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the taking is both part of the witnessed scene and completed by the source-place phrase that follows.
topics.reason: The passive verb takes {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) plus the place phrase as its complement, and the seeing frame makes seizure visible.

topics.headline: agent withheld but discourse pressure remains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical passive preserves patienthood and agent omission, while outside parallels only frame the unnamed taker by contrast.
topics.reason: The variant nominal row and 11:102 contrast are useful, but local grammar suppresses the agent and keeps {{ar:أُخِذُوا۟}} ({{tr:ukhidhū}}) as a passive event.

topics.headline: glottal onset marks seizure impact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the return from nominal verdict to event as an audible impact at the passive verb’s onset.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is locally tied to the surface onset of the passive verb after the connector.

words.gloss_range: source preposition governing the place phrase as the origin of extraction
words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the following place phrase the source of extraction, not a vague setting. After the passive verb, the ayah does not name an agent; it completes the event spatially, from a place, and only then lets {{ar:قَرِيبٍۢ}} ({{tr:qarībin}}) disclose that the source is near. The nasal bond in {{ar:مِن مَّكَانٍۢ}} ({{tr:min makānin}}) matches the syntactic bond between preposition and place.

topics.headline: place phrase marks origin of seizure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that seizure is described as extraction from a source-point, not simply as occurring somewhere.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the place noun the prepositional complement of {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) after the passive verb.

topics.headline: passive event completed by source before nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the passive event is completed by spatial source rather than by naming the taker, and that nearness is delayed to the end.
topics.reason: The passive agent is omitted while the {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) phrase follows as complement, so the structure supports spatial completion.

topics.headline: preposition and place fuse audibly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source relation is heard as tightly joined before the final adjective arrives.
topics.reason: The formal rows are local to the adjacent {{ar:مِن مَّكَانٍۢ}} ({{tr:min makānin}}) sequence and match the syntactic dependency.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive noun of place functioning as the source-point of seizure
words.root_gloss_range: being, coming-to-be, state, and place; local noun-of-place pattern selects situated location while retaining position/status pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: source preposition governing the place noun
adjective controlled by the place noun

words.prose: {{ar:مَّكَانٍۢ}} ({{tr:makānin}}) gives the seizure a real but unnamed source-place. It is genitive after {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}), not the thing seized, and it controls {{ar:قَرِيبٍۢ}} ({{tr:qarībin}}) as its adjective; the phrase first establishes place, then reveals nearness. The k-w-n background lets location feel like situated existence, but the noun-of-place form keeps location primary. Its recurrence with near/far language in 34:52 and 34:53 opens a local spatial axis, while the contrast with a far place in 41:44 sharpens how immediate this source is.

topics.headline: indefinite place grounds extraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the capture-source is real and grammatical, yet unnamed, so proximity matters more than geography.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite genitive after {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) and functions as the source complement of the passive taking.

topics.headline: place binds the final nearness adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that nearness is grammatically locked to the place noun and heard in the shared indefinite genitive cadence.
topics.reason: Agreement evidence identifies {{ar:قَرِيبٍۢ}} ({{tr:qarībin}}) as the adjective of the place noun, and both forms share genitive indefiniteness.

topics.headline: being-root pressure becomes situated place
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the place is not abstract coordinates only; it is the position in which the panicked group is found, while the noun form keeps the sense spatial.
topics.reason: The k-w-n root field supports being and state, but local morphology is a noun of place governed by {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}), so state/formation claims are preserved only as situated-place pressure.

topics.headline: place phrase opens near/far reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this near source-place starts a spatial axis that the following verses reverse into far-place impossibility.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows give concrete references for the near/far place pattern, especially 34:52, 34:53, and the contrast with 41:44.

topics.headline: source appears before final nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ending as spatial architecture: source first, final nearness last.
topics.reason: The phrase after the passive verb builds a source complement followed by an adjective, supporting the staging rows.

words.gloss_range: genitive indefinite qualitative adjective marking the source-place as near
words.root_gloss_range: nearness in place, time, relation, access, or approach; local agreement with the place noun selects spatial nearness with immediacy pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: source-place noun modified by the final adjective

words.prose: {{ar:قَرِيبٍۢ}} ({{tr:qarībin}}) is the final reveal of the source phrase. It agrees with {{ar:مَّكَانٍۢ}} ({{tr:makānin}}), so nearness is the place’s quality, not a detached adverb, and the qualitative adjective states sufficient closeness rather than a comparison. The root can cover spatial, temporal, relational, and access-nearness; here the place noun makes it spatial, while the no-escape context makes it feel immediately reachable. Against mercy-nearness in 7:56 and the divine nearness of 34:50, this closing word turns nearness into exposure; against 34:52, it sets up the near/far reversal. The paired genitive indefinite -in endings bind source and nearness as one closing cadence.

topics.headline: nearness belongs to the place
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final nearness is grammatically attached to the source-place, not floating as a temporal or general adverb.
topics.reason: Agreement evidence makes the adjective qualify the place noun in genitive indefiniteness.

topics.headline: ayah lands on proximity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not close on seizure itself but on the nearness that makes escape-space disappear.
topics.reason: The adjective is postposed after the source noun and is the final word, so the structural and closure rows are locally supported.

topics.headline: spatial closeness carries access-pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local phrase selects spatial nearness, while the wider root range adds immediacy and access-pressure without replacing the place reading.
topics.reason: The head noun is a place noun, so temporal, relational, and devotional branches are narrowed to pressure around the selected spatial adjective.

topics.headline: nearness shifts from mercy or access to threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a value-shift in nearness: what can mark mercy or divine accessibility elsewhere becomes capture-proximity here.
topics.reason: The contrast rows give concrete anchors in 7:56 and 34:50 and are coherent with the local source-place adjective.

topics.headline: near capture anticipates far impossibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final near-place word is answered by the far-place reversal in the next ayah.
topics.reason: The forward boundary row specifically connects the final nearness of 34:51 to the far-place language in 34:52.

topics.headline: source and nearness close as one acoustic unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paired indefinite endings binding place and nearness in the closing sound of the ayah.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is supported by the matching genitive indefinite endings of the noun and adjective.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ, فَزِعُوا, فَلَا فَوْتَ, and أُخِذُوا.
baseline_models.mechanism: A scene is opened to sight, panic erupts, evasive reach is expressly canceled, and passive seizure completes the sequence. Perception, affect, lost mobility, and capture occur as one compressed event.

activation_trace.role: Direct or insight-like perception supplies the witnessing frame in which the event becomes present.
Terror and recoil from danger supply the subjects' abrupt affective contraction.
Failure of attainment or escape supplies the explicit closure of evasive reach.
Seizing a captive supplies the external act that terminates the panic sequence.

changed_reading.before: A report that frightened people are caught.
changed_reading.after: A disclosed capture sequence in which panic coincides with the extinction of evasive reach and culminates in arrest.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The adjacency of فَلَا فَوْتَ and مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The negated فوت can image not only failed escape but the absence of a usable interval; مكان locates the operation, and قريب places its source already within reach. Capture therefore need not conclude a chase.

activation_trace.role: A gap or opening between two things supplies the spatial interval that the negation removes.
Place and emplacement supply a concrete operational site for the seizure.
Nearness rather than distance makes the captors' reach immediate.

changed_reading.before: Pursuit closes distance until the people can no longer flee.
changed_reading.after: No chase has to close distance: seizure operates from an already near site where no spatial interval functions as escape.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The cluster فَلَا فَوْتَ, أُخِذُوا, and قَرِيبٍ.
baseline_models.mechanism: A form of فوت evokes an end arriving before intended repair, أخذ permits being held answerable, and قرب permits temporal imminence. The physical capture can therefore coexist with a sudden accountability reading.

activation_trace.role: A sudden terminal arrival that precludes a final intended act supplies the event's no-more-time quality.
Being taken to account for what issued from a person supplies a juridical layer to the seizure.
An approaching time or promise supplies imminence alongside spatial proximity.

changed_reading.before: The verse depicts only bodily apprehension.
changed_reading.after: The bodily seizure also reads as sudden accountability whose near arrival leaves no interval for repair.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier, the same root occurs in a passive construction where terror is cleared from hearts and speech resumes; at the focus, terror erupts and is followed by no escape and seizure. The focus panic thus marks the failure of the earlier release pattern.

activation_trace.role: The focus occurrence supplies terror as the immediate onset of closure.
Removal of fear supplies the contrasting possibility of a heart being cleared so that response becomes possible.

structural_cues: 34:23 places the passive fear-root construction before resumed dialogue, whereas 34:51 places active plural panic immediately before فَلَا فَوْتَ.
The same root is followed first by opened speech and later by closed mobility.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated root and opposite continuations; I infer a reversal from cleared fear to fear without clearance. A live alternative is that these are independent fear scenes rather than phases of one pattern.

changed_reading.before: Their panic is a generic reaction to danger.
changed_reading.after: Their panic signals that the surah's earlier fear-clearing possibility is no longer available: affect is not released into speech but sealed into capture.

context_deltas.mechanism: The questioned promise is assigned a fixed appointment at which neither delay nor advance is possible. That temporal bracket activates the focus's no-fوت and near-time branches: seizure arrives on a non-negotiable schedule, not merely at a nearby location.

activation_trace.role: Sudden terminal arrival supplies the loss of any last postponement or repair.
Temporal nearness supplies the focus event's imminence.
A promise bounded by a time or place supplies the fixed appointment governing the event.
Deferral to a later time supplies the temporal maneuver explicitly denied.
Advancing ahead supplies the opposite temporal maneuver, also explicitly denied.

structural_cues: 34:29 asks when the promise will occur; 34:30 answers with a fixed appointment and symmetric negations of delay and advance.
34:51 compresses panic, no escape, and seizure under إِذْ, presenting the appointed instant as already occurring.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a fixed-time pair and the focus's sudden sequence; I infer that temporal non-slippage is one mechanism of فَلَا فَوْتَ. The alternative is to keep فوت purely spatial and the appointment only thematic.

changed_reading.before: Capture happens suddenly at an unspecified moment.
changed_reading.after: Capture realizes a fixed appointment: no escape includes the impossibility of moving its time backward or forward.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذْ tableau shows wrongdoers held in place; they later see punishment as necks are bound, and opponents of the signs are made present in punishment. The focus repeats the viewing frame and condenses this grammar of immobilization into no escape and seizure.

activation_trace.role: Perception supplies the focus tableau's disclosed viewpoint.
Captive seizure supplies the culmination of the immobilization sequence.
A matching act of seeing supplies the earlier tableau that the focus construction recalls.
Fixed standing and remaining in a place supply the first form of compelled immobility.
The subjects' own sight of punishment turns disclosure from observer-facing scene into experienced recognition.
A collar that binds an organ supplies material restraint.
The neck supplies the bodily site on which restraint is fixed.
Forced presence and nearness supply movement into the judgment space rather than movement away from it.

structural_cues: The exact frame وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذْ occurs at 34:31 and 34:51.
The passive forms مَوْقُوفُونَ, مُحْضَرُونَ, and أُخِذُوا distribute agency away from the captured subjects.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated visual framing and several compelled states; I infer an escalating grammar from stopped, to bound, to made present, to seized. These may instead be parallel judgment images without temporal escalation.

changed_reading.before: 34:51 is an isolated scene of ambush.
changed_reading.after: 34:51 culminates a recurring disclosed immobilization: the subjects are stopped, materially bound, forced into presence, and finally seized.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier proximity is a valued relation that wealth and children cannot produce; immediately before the focus, divine hearing is paired with nearness. The focus then turns nearness into the range from which seizure operates, reversing sought relational proximity into unavoidable exposure.

activation_trace.role: Operative nearness supplies the range from which seizure is immediate.
Approach to God through an accepted means supplies nearness as a sought and evaluated relation.
Perceptive hearing supplies the preceding nearness with an awareness relation, not distance alone.
The explicit divine attribute of nearness supplies the immediate contextual pole for the focus's nearby place.

structural_cues: 34:37 denies that possessions and children can bring their owners near, while faith and right action mark the exception.
34:50 ends with سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ and 34:51 ends with مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies evaluated nearness and the adjacent hearing-nearness/focus-near pair; I infer a reversal from chosen approach to unavoidable exposure. The live alternative is that the focus adjective is only local and carries no relational force.

changed_reading.before: Near describes only the captors' physical location.
changed_reading.after: Near also carries a value reversal: proximity that cannot be bought or mediated becomes unavoidable exposure within the range of hearing and seizure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus says they are taken from a near place; the next ayah asks how they could perform reaching from a far place. The mirrored place phrases reverse agency: seizure can reach them without interval, but their belated reaching toward belief or rescue cannot cross the distance.

activation_trace.role: Taking and bringing something into one's grasp supply successful reach exercised upon the subjects.
The focus place supplies one pole of the explicit near/far spatial mirror.
Nearness makes the seizure's reach effective.
Extending to take and successfully reach something supplies the agency now questioned or denied.
The repeated place construction supplies the matching second pole of the spatial mirror.
Distance opposed to nearness makes their attempted reach ineffective.

structural_cues: The adjacent phrases مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ and مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ repeat preposition, noun, and adjective slot while reversing the adjective.
Passive أُخِذُوا marks successful action upon them; the rhetorical وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ questions action available to them.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exact near/far constructional mirror and opposed grasping roles; I infer an asymmetry of agency and reach. The alternative is to treat the two locations as unrelated descriptions.

changed_reading.before: They happen to be captured nearby.
changed_reading.after: They are completely reachable by seizure while their own belated attempt to reach belief or rescue is stranded at a distance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing ayah installs a separator between the subjects and what they desire. This converts the focus's no-escape statement from blocked locomotion alone into a broader relation of non-attainment: the desired object remains across an imposed divide.

activation_trace.role: Failed attainment or escape supplies the focus's general closure of access.
An intervening barrier that separates two things supplies the mechanism that makes access fail.
Repeated between-positions supply an explicit relation of separation between subject and object.
The self's pull toward what it desires supplies the inaccessible target across the barrier.

structural_cues: 34:54 follows the near capture and far-reaching statements with a passive barrier construction.
The doubled بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ grammatically places the parties on opposite sides of the imposed separation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies no escape, failed far-reaching, and then an imposed subject-object barrier; I infer that the barrier completes the focus's closure mechanism. The alternative is that 34:54 concerns desire alone and should not broaden the locomotion of 34:51.

changed_reading.before: No escape means they cannot run away from capture.
changed_reading.after: No escape also means no attainment: an imposed divide prevents them from reaching what the self now wants.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads a physical-looking capture through an epistemic geometry of projection. It remains anchored in the focus's seeing and near-place language and in the packet's repeated casting, unseen, and far-place sequence. Downstream prose should mark it as a spatial-epistemic analogy, not claim that قذف lexically governs 34:51.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: تَرَىٰ and مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ, contrasted with the casting and far-place language of 34:48 and 34:53.

activation_trace.role: Actual or insight-like sight supplies the replacement of remote conjecture by disclosed presence.
Nearness supplies the collapsed distance at which consequences become operative.
Projection or casting across distance supplies truth's forceful arrival into the sequence.
The repeated casting image supplies the subjects' contrary act of projecting claims from afar.
What is hidden from sight supplies the inaccessible object of their projection.
Distance opposed to nearness supplies the epistemic gap from which they had been casting.

changed_reading.before: The focus depicts only a nearby physical arrest.
changed_reading.after: The arrest also images an epistemic distance collapse: remote projection toward the unseen ends when the scene becomes visible and consequence acts at near range.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the focus form ordinarily presents terror, while another live branch of the same root concerns turning to refuge or aid. It remains anchored in فَزِعُوا and فَلَا فَوْتَ; downstream prose should describe a possible refuge reflex within panic, not translate فَزِعُوا as 'they sought refuge.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The immediate coupling of فَزِعُوا with فَلَا فَوْتَ and أُخِذُوا.

activation_trace.role: Turning toward a refuge when danger strikes supplies a latent action impulse inside the panic.
Failed access or escape prevents that refuge impulse from reaching an effective shelter.
Capture terminates the attempted orientation toward safety before it can function.

changed_reading.before: Panic is only an internal emotional state.
changed_reading.after: Panic may include an abortive reflex toward refuge, but no reachable shelter intervenes before seizure.

strongest_changes: The 34:23 fear-root reversal changes panic from generic emotion into fear for which the earlier clearing pattern is unavailable.
The exact 34:51-52 near/far place mirror changes capture into an asymmetry: they are reachable by seizure but cannot reach from belated distance.
The fixed appointment of 34:30 and imposed barrier of 34:54 extend فَلَا فَوْتَ across time, space, and desired attainment.
Repeated seeing, stopping, binding, forced presence, and passive seizure make 34:51 the culmination of a disclosed immobilization pattern.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context activated several coexisting geometries around the focus: visual disclosure, juridical immobilization, fixed time, valued versus coercive proximity, successful taking versus failed reaching, and an epistemic near/far collapse. The adjacent 34:50-54 sequence sharpened these without reducing them to one final interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ is primarily a literal capture site, temporal imminence, relational nearness, or deliberately supports several layers.
Whether the fear clearing at 34:23 is meant as a direct reversal of 34:51 or is only a reusable root contrast.
How much weight the exploratory casting/unseen geometry should carry beyond the explicit near/far constructional mirror.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Alarm collapses the escape interval.** `ف ز ع/B001` is alarm before danger, `ف و ت/B001` being beyond reach, `ء خ ذ/B003` capture, and `ق ر ب/B001` nearness. Alarm is followed by explicit negation of missing, then passive capture from a near place. Alarm marks recognition, no-escape removes the gap, and nearness makes capture immediate. The packet states the sequence; I infer that the distance imagined by denial disappears at recognition. The ayah reads nearness not as comfort but as the end of maneuvering room.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 34:52 made the lost escape interval into lost grasp, shifting from being reached by capture to being unable to reach desired belief.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Escape eliminated by capture from nearness.** `ف و ت B001` supplies missing or being beyond reach, `ء خ ذ B003` capture and captivity, and `ق ر ب B001` nearness. Panic is followed by negated escape and immediate seizure from a near place; 34:52-53 repeat a far place for their failed reaching and conjectural casting. The branches assign nearness to effective agency and distance to failed agency. The packet supplies the contrast; I infer that the spatial strategy they presumed is inverted. The scene reads as authority already within reach of them while their own reach has become remote.

2. **Alarm finds no refuge.** `ف ز ع B003` supplies turning to a refuge in alarm, and `ف و ت B004` a gap between two things. The sequence denies escape before any refuge-gap can open; 34:54 will install a barrier only between them and what they desire. The branches assign panic an attempted refuge motion and no-escape the closure of available interval. The packet supplies alarm and capture; I infer that the normal refuge response has no spatial outlet. Panic reads as motion without a destination.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 34:52 supplied the exact counter-motion: after they are reached from near, they try to reach belief from far. 34:54 then closed even the refuge-object with an intervening barrier, completing the failed-motion reading.

findings.text: Korku anında hayal edilen kaçış aralığı kapanır; yakınlık bu kez rahatlık değil, yakalamanın hiçbir manevra payı bırakmadan gerçekleşmesidir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P4: Deferred Belief Becomes a Geometry of Capture
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Once panic arrives, the former freedom to defer is translated into spatial relations: seizure is near, belief is sought from far away, speculative speech is projected toward the unseen, and a barrier closes access to desire.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The `ق ذ ف` field reverses the effective projection of truth in 34:48 into distant verbal throwing at the unseen in 34:53, making distance a difference in epistemic warrant.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Near Seizure Eliminates Escape
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Panic erupts, escape becomes impossible, and capture occurs from a position already close at hand.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: panic (`quranic:root_001152:B001/m01`), failure to elude (`quranic:root_001183:B001/m01`), taking captive (`quranic:root_000018:B003/m01`), spatial proximity (`quranic:root_001212:B001/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The scene collapses the imagined interval required for escape. Capture is near not only geographically but temporally: no further postponement remains available.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görmeyi hem gözle algılama hem de gözün işlevine benzetilen içsel kavrayış olarak kuruyor. Doğrudan göz tanıklığı bu çekirdeğin duyusal gerçekleşimidir; zihinsel görüş, uyku düşü ve başkalarına görünme amacı bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği görsel ya da içsel algıdır; belirli söz öbekleri ve bakma çabası ayrı kullanımlar olarak tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın görme çekirdeği ile doğrudan göz tanıklığını ve görmeye çalışma bildiren bağlı kullanımlar birbirine karıştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi gözle ya da göz işlevi gören içsel kavrayışla algılamaktır. Gözün eriştiği yerde doğrudan görme, bu anlamın duyusal ve tanıklığa dayalı gerçekleşimidir.

facets.statement: Görülebilir bir şeyi gözle veya benzer bir içsel kavrayışla algılama.
Bir şeyi gözün eriştiği yerde doğrudan ve tanık olarak görme.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, gözle görmeyi temel alır ve bazı anlatımlarda bu algıyı içsel kavrayışa kadar genişletir; doğrudan göz tanıklığı özellikle belirtilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ortak ekseni, bir konu hakkında zihinsel bir yargı veya görüş oluşturmaktır. Bilme ya da sanma değeri belirli tümce yapılarında, danışma ise başka birinin görüşünü istemede ortaya çıkar; bunlar yalın çekirdeğin eş düzeyli anlamları sayılmamalıdır.
